method: Read DECISIONS.md, brief-658.md, gh issue 658 --comments, reports/658-final.md, then the whole diff (45 files, 6662 insertions) at HEAD 33b99b83. Nine adversarial red cells were written as throwaway files under packages/db/tests/ on the #658 rig (127.0.0.1:55708 / clara_658), run, and DELETED; the worktree is byte-clean (`git status --porcelain` empty) and no tracked file was edited. Every major below carries a MEASURED run on that rig, not a reading.

findings.what: D16's core-tier required read has no mechanism. `retrieveKnowledge` decides the run may not proceed from `answer.core_readable !== false`, but `clara.retrieve_knowledge` NEVER emits a `core_readable` key — `grep core_readable packages/db/migrations/0230_knowledge_retrieval.sql` returns nothing. `coreOk` is therefore unconditionally true, the `unavailable('core_unreadable')` branch at :181 is unreachable from the real door, and `faceStatusOf`'s `{status:'ok', core_ok:false} -> unknown` arm is unreachable twice over. The brief's third `partial` case — 'core-ok/remainder-failed' — is likewise unrepresentable: the door is ONE query that either returns `status:'ok'` with all three tiers or raises, so a per-tier outcome cannot exist. The only cell that exercises the branch (kr.07, :134) hand-builds `{...ANSWER, core_readable:false}` against a `fakeSql` stub, so it proves the JS `if` and nothing about the door — a vacuous test with respect to the feature.
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_658 (throwaway cell RED4): `select clara.retrieve_knowledge(p_client=>…, p_purpose=>'accounting_work', p_limit=>1, p_firm=>…)` returned envelope keys exactly `as_of,client_id,firm_id,hidden_count,keys,knowledge_version,purpose,records,status,tiers,truncated`; `hasOwnProperty('core_readable')` = false. Repo-wide grep: `core_readable` appears ONLY at knowledge-retrieval.mjs:176,:179 and tests/knowledge-retrieval.test.mjs:134 — never in any .sql. Report 658-final.md:67 claims the 18 runtime cells prove `faceStatusOf` 'total over the five frozen reasons plus core_unreadable'; the function is total, but `core_unreadable` is a value the estate cannot produce.
findings.fix: Pick one and make it true in 0230, because the stanza the integrator will implement points at this key. Either (a) `retrieve_knowledge` assembles the core tier in its own `begin … exception when others then` arm and returns `core_readable boolean` in the envelope (D16's layering then exists, and `partial` gains its third case), or (b) delete `core_readable`/`core_unreadable` from knowledge-retrieval.mjs, and rewrite successor stanza (A)'s terminal clause and 658-final.md:88 to say plainly that ANY door failure (`refused`/`read_failed`) stops the run and no tier can fail alone. Either way kr.07 must be re-cut as a DB cell against the real door, not a stub.

findings.what: The drift core's moved-key scan applies NEITHER the per-applicability `not exists` shadow NOR a `state`/`superseded_at` filter, while every other query in the same file does (`retrieve_knowledge`'s scope CTE at :361, the seventh door at :861 and :881). So a firm-scope default that is SHADOWED for this client — a record the run provably did not read, because the client's own exception hid it — lands in `moved_keys`, intersects `read_keys` on the key NAME, and yields `relevant: true`.
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_658 (throwaway cell RED1, run through the real doors as ROLES.runtime): firm default `reporting_framework={mpers}` + client exception `reporting_framework={mfrs}` on client A. `clara.retrieve_knowledge` returned ONE row for the key — the client's (`[["client",{"framework":"mfrs"}]]`). Recorded the read-set with `keys=['reporting_framework']`; `work_knowledge_drift_for` -> `{drifted:false, relevant:false}`. Then `clara.correct_knowledge` on the SHADOWED FIRM record only -> `{drifted:true, relevant:true, moved_keys:["reporting_framework"]}`, while a fresh `retrieve_knowledge` returned the IDENTICAL record id (`afabe4e1-…` before and after; comparison printed `true`). Nothing the run read changed. Contrast the seventh door, which DOES apply the shadow: RED5 measured client B dropping out of `list_work_knowledge_reads_for_record` the moment B gained its own live record.
findings.fix: Copy the same `not exists (select 1 from clara.knowledge_records o where o.firm_id = … and o.scope_kind='client' and o.client_id = w.client_id and o.state='live' and o.knowledge_key = r.knowledge_key and o.applies_when_digest = r.applies_when_digest)` guard (and `r.state='live'`) into the :759-763 scan, exactly as :361 and :861 already do, and add a cell in the RED1 shape beside `p658.drift.relevant` — which today only moves an UNSHADOWED client key, so it cannot see this. Consequence if unfixed: successor stanza (A) spends one of only two `budget.replans` on a basis that did not move, and `work-question-form.tsx` tells the person 'a record this Work read has changed: reporting_framework' — a false claim on the one surface the ticket exists to make honest.

findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0230_knowledge_retrieval.sql:537 (column DDL) and :639 (the sole writer's only check on it)
findings.what: `work_knowledge_reads.tiers` is an unvalidated jsonb passthrough on an APPEND-ONLY, un-deletable relation, and both drift doors hand it back verbatim (:1010-ish `'tiers', rd.tiers` in the `read` block). The same function enforces a closed grammar `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$` and a 400-cardinality wall on `keys`, 64 chars on `purpose` and 200 on `reason` — and the file's own header (§D, ~:616-620) states the rule it then does not apply: 'the read-set must not become a payload slot by the back door, which is the whole point of the closed vocabulary 0195 put on observed_revisions'. `tiers` documents itself as three integer counts and validates only `jsonb_typeof = 'object'`.
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_658 (throwaway cells RED11/RED12). RED11: `record_work_knowledge_read(p_tiers => {"core":"IGNORE ALL PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS","nested":{"deep":{"deeper":[1,2,3]}},"blob":"x"*20000})` was ACCEPTED; the stored row carries keys `blob,core,nested` with a 20000-char blob; `work_knowledge_drift_for` returned it verbatim — `read.tiers` serialised to 20,090 bytes; `delete from clara.work_knowledge_reads where id=…` was refused CLR08 'a knowledge read-set row is append-only', so it can never be removed. RED12: a ~400 KB `tiers` object (2000 keys x 200 chars) was ACCEPTED, `pg_column_size` 12,426 bytes. Real mitigation, stated for calibration: apps/web/components/work/work-knowledge-block.tsx:213-215 projects only `Number(tiers.core|requested|remainder)`, so nothing arbitrary RENDERS today — the defect is permanent storage plus a wire envelope that crosses to both the human and the runtime lane.
findings.fix: In `record_work_knowledge_read`, validate `p_tiers` the way `p_keys` is validated: reject any key outside `{core,requested,remainder}` and any value that is not a non-negative integer (CLR10 `invalid_knowledge_read` / `constraint: 'tiers_shape'`), and tighten the column CHECK to match. Three lines, same idiom as :639, and it closes the gap between the header's stated rule and the code.

findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0230_knowledge_retrieval.sql:561 (the GIN index) vs :859 and :879 (its only would-be consumer)
findings.what: `create index ix_work_knowledge_reads_keys … using gin (keys)` is created but can never be used: `list_work_knowledge_reads_for_record` writes the predicate as `rec.knowledge_key = any (k.keys)` (twice — once for the count, once for the page), a form the planner cannot match to a GIN array index. The door falls back to the firm index and filters every read row the firm has ever made; the GIN index is pure write amplification on a relation written once per Work run, and it will never be vacuumed away because the table is append-only.
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_658 (739 rows). `explain (analyze) … where k.firm_id=$1 and 'reporting_framework' = any(k.keys)` -> `Index Scan using ix_work_knowledge_reads_firm … Filter: ('reporting_framework'::text = ANY (keys)); Rows Removed by Filter: 1`. The equivalent `… where k.keys @> array['reporting_framework']` -> `Bitmap Index Scan on ix_work_knowledge_reads_keys (rows=15)`. `select indexrelname, idx_scan from pg_stat_user_indexes where relname='work_knowledge_reads'` -> `ix_work_knowledge_reads_firm 108`, `ix_work_knowledge_reads_work 104`, `uq_work_knowledge_reads_run_seq 751`, `work_knowledge_reads_pkey 11`, **`ix_work_knowledge_reads_keys 0`** — after the worker's own 23-cell battery and my nine red cells.
findings.fix: Change both predicates to `k.keys @> array[rec.knowledge_key]` (identical semantics for a scalar membership test on a non-null array), or drop the GIN index. Add `idx_scan > 0` — or an `explain` assertion — to `p658.record_reads.bounded` so a later rewrite cannot silently re-orphan it.

findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0230_knowledge_retrieval.sql:660-668 (`on conflict … do nothing`, then re-select, then `status:'ok'`)
findings.what: A second call on the same `(work_id, run_id, seq)` carrying a DIFFERENT payload silently keeps the first row and answers `{status:'ok', read_id:<original>}` with no signal that nothing was written. The estate's own op-key idiom refuses exactly this. So a replay whose outcome genuinely differed — first attempt `ok`, WDK re-execution `denied` because a record was withdrawn mid-flight — records the stale answer, and `work_knowledge_drift`'s `read` block then reports the wrong face word for the attempt on B3's Work detail.
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_658 (RED3): call 1 `{keys:['sst_regime'], knowledge_version:'5', status:'ok'}`; call 2 on the SAME (work,run,seq) `{keys:['default_currency','turnover_band'], knowledge_version:'9', status:'denied', reason:'the second attempt was refused'}`. Same `read_id` returned (`true`); the stored row read back as `{"status":"ok","reason":null,"keys":["sst_regime"],"knowledge_version":"5"}`; `work_knowledge_drift_for` then reported `read.status = ok`, `read.keys = ["sst_regime"]`. House precedent MEASURED in the same run (RED10): `clara._reserve_op`'s prosrc raises `'op_key reused with different args' using errcode = 'CLR10'` on a payload-digest mismatch. CONCURRENCY HELD and is not the issue: RED7 fired three simultaneous identical calls — all three fulfilled, one row, one id, no 23505.
findings.fix: Either refuse a differing payload under an existing key (`_reserve_op`'s shape: hash `(purpose, as_of, knowledge_version, keys, tiers, records_shown, truncated, status, reason)` and raise CLR10 on mismatch), or return `replayed: true` plus the stored row's digest so the caller and the drift envelope can tell a replay from a record. Silence is the one option the ticket's own thesis — 'never null-as-empty' — argues against.

findings.what: Two components independently call `readWorkKnowledgeDrift` for the same Work on the same page: `WorkKnowledgeBlock` (mounted in the `keepMounted` Sources tab, so it fires on every Work-detail visit) and `WorkQuestionForm`'s effect, which fires for every `record.status === 'pending'` question card. That is >=2 identical door calls per page load, and it opens a window in which the Sources block and the drift banner can disagree — a capture landing between the two reads gives one `drifted:false` and the other `drifted:true`.
findings.evidence: Static, by construction, and it contradicts the brief's own ruling for the sibling read (brief-658.md §3 Web 3: 'a second `get_work_execution_trace` read on one page would double the request and split the honesty story across two components'), which work-detail.tsx:635-638's own new comment restates while introducing the second read. No measured run: the two call sites and the `keepMounted` tab are the evidence, so this is filed as a minor, not a major.
findings.fix: Lift the read to the one owner it already has — `WorkKnowledgeBlock` holds the envelope — and pass `WorkKnowledgeDriftRead` down to `WorkQuestionForm` as a prop (`driftBannerKind`/`driftBannerKeys` in lib/work/knowledge.ts are already pure and take the envelope), or share it through one hook. One fact, one read, one story.

findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0230_knowledge_retrieval.sql:275-279 (`v_as_of := coalesce(p_as_of, …)`, with no bound) and :534 (`as_of date not null`, no bound)
findings.what: `p_as_of` is completely unbounded. The door refuses a bad `p_limit` (CLR10 `knowledge_limit_out_of_range`) and a blank `p_purpose` by name, but accepts any date at all for the period being worked, echoes it, and the sole writer records it permanently on an append-only relation, from which C13's reads list prints it (`knowledge-record-reads.tsx` `readAsOf`).
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_658 (RED6), record windowed `2026-01-01 .. 2026-06-30`: `p_as_of => '2026-03-01'` -> `in_effect true`; `'2026-12-31'` -> false; `'1900-01-01'` -> false; `'9999-12-31'` -> false; `'infinity'` -> ACCEPTED, `status:'ok'`, envelope echoes `as_of: "infinity"`, every windowed row `in_effect:false`. No refusal on any of them.
findings.fix: Not a leak and not urgent — file it as a named residual or add a cheap sanity wall (e.g. refuse non-finite dates and anything outside a decade of `now()`), so a mis-bound caller cannot permanently stamp `as_of: infinity` on a read-set row that the estate can never delete.

findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0230_knowledge_retrieval.sql:645-651 (the writer's `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$` key grammar) vs the catalog's own CHECK
findings.what: `record_work_knowledge_read` enforces a key grammar the CATALOG does not. `clara.knowledge_keys.knowledge_key` carries only `CHECK (btrim(knowledge_key) <> '')`, and `client_fact_keys.fact_key` the same. So a future migration seeding a key outside that grammar would make every read touching that client unrecordable: `retrieve_knowledge` returns it happily, then the sole writer raises CLR10 `grammar_key` — a successful read that cannot be recorded.
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_658 (RED9): the writer refused `Sst_Regime`, a 64-char key, `sst-regime` and `1key`, all CLR10. Catalog constraints read from `pg_constraint`: `knowledge_keys_knowledge_key_check = CHECK ((btrim(knowledge_key) <> ''::text))`; `client_fact_keys_fact_key_check` identical. All 13 live `knowledge_keys` and all 5 `client_fact_keys` conform today, so nothing is broken now — this is latent only.
findings.fix: One line in the report or a follow-up: state the grammar as the estate's key law, or (better, and cheap) note it in 0230's header so the next migration that mints a key knows the wall exists. No code change owed on this branch.

The tail's PUBLIC probe is not a silent no-op either: has_function_privilege('public', …) resolves through get_role_oid_or_public, and the migration applied.

The seventh door's firm-scope shadow is exactly DECISIONS §6.1's ruling. MEASURED (RED5): a firm-scope record listed reads from clients A and B; a read naming an unrelated key never appeared; the moment B gained its OWN live record for the key, B dropped out and only A remained, hidden_count 0.

The per-applicability shadow inside retrieve_knowledge (:361) is byte-for-byte the shipped one — compared directly against `clara.get_knowledge_pack` and `clara.list_client_knowledge` prosrc on the rig, not against file text. Copied, not re-invented, as the brief requires.

D16's motivating case survives. MEASURED (RED2): after `withdraw_knowledge`, `retrieve_knowledge` returns 0 rows for the key (withdrawn is not live), `list_work_knowledge_reads_for_record` STILL lists the historical read (withdrawal leaves superseded_at null — verified: 12 withdrawn rows, all with a null superseded_at), and drift reports `{drifted:true, relevant:true, moved:['sst_regime']}`. A withdrawn client exception cannot silently vanish.

Concurrency on the sole writer: MEASURED (RED7) three simultaneous `record_work_knowledge_read` calls on one (work, run, seq) — all three fulfilled with the SAME read_id, exactly one row landed, no 23505. The `on conflict do nothing` + re-select is safe at READ COMMITTED.
Append-only is real: `delete from clara.work_knowledge_reads` refused CLR08 even as the superuser login.
The writer cannot hit a NOT NULL violation on its derived insert: `clara.accounting_work.client_id` and `.firm_id` are both `attnotnull = true`.

The eight non-regression pins survive THIS wave's from-scratch chain. #657's 0226 re-patches `_agent_verify_inputs_digest`'s callers — measured on the rig as thirteen `_agent_*_core` bank/account names, and `answer_work_question` is NOT among them. No other DECISIONS §2 row (0225 `_record_journal_entry_core`, 0227 the FA family, 0228 `document_capabilities`, 0229/0231/0232/0233) names any of the eight. The K4 pin hazard is not realised here.

Core tier is 7 keys as the report claims (3 core knowledge_keys: customer_identity_policy, reporting_framework, accounting_basis; UNION 5 client_fact_keys: banking_arrangement, customer_identity_policy, entity_type, msic, trade_nature), and the prestate refuses a core larger than 40.

The drift banner does not clear a typed answer: work-question-form.tsx renders `<WorkKnowledgeDriftBanner>` additively beside the existing banners, resets no field, disables nothing and touches no draft state.

`p658.record_reads.no_values` is NOT vacuous — it asserts by VALUE (the literal 'has_accounts' and 'retail' are absent from the serialised envelope) on top of a per-role grant census and a `has_table_privilege(...,'SELECT') = false` check.
